blocks.text: Entertainment·New

The 2027 Grammy nominees for best new artist dropped Monday, putting a spotlight on who's reshaping the music scene. If you want to keep your playlist fresh — or at least know what everyone in the group chat is talking about — here are the names shaping the conversation.
Not familiar with their music? Don't worry, we've got you covered
The 2027 Grammy nominees for best new artist dropped Monday, putting a spotlight on who's reshaping the music scene.

Despite what the name suggests, a nominee doesn't actually have to be brand new to qualify. Some might even argue "breakthrough artist" would be a better fit for the nominees. With new rules allowing artists to be submitted up to four times instead of three, this year gave both artists putting in the work for years as well as some fresh faces their moment.
Past winners have gone on to become global icons, such as Christina Aguilera, Adele and Billie Eilish. And recent recipients include Olivia Rodrigo, Chappell Roan and Olivia Dean.
So if you want to keep your playlist fresh — or at least know what everyone in the group chat is talking about — here are the names shaping the conversation.
Angine de Poitrine

The Quebec alien-like math rock duo that went from underground favourites to international sensations, seemingly overnight. From Saguenay, Que., the masked, polka-dot-costumed performers build their microtonal sound live with looping pedals while wearing oversized papier mâché heads. The two started 2026 under the radar and have since performed with Shania Twain and opened for Jack White. The anonymous duo — known as Khn and Klek de Poitrine — also picked up three other Grammy nominations on Monday, including best rock performance, best rock album and best alternative music performance.
The hit you might know: Fabienk.
Don Toliver

You may know him from his breakout 2018 feature Can't Say on Travis Scott's ASTROWORLD. The Houston, Texas born rapper has been releasing music for over a decade. Known for his psychedelic trap/R&B sound, he's collaborated with artists ranging from SZA, Baby Keem, Kali Uchis, Kaytranada and Drake. If there was a big rap release, he probably had a hand in it. Toliver is the leading hip-hop artist at this year's Grammys with five nominations for his album Octane and hit single E85.
The hit you might know: E85.
Ella Langley

It's been a huge year for the 27-year-old artist from Alabama. Her breakout hit Choosin' Texas holds the record for longest-running No. 1 in Billboard Hot 100 history. Langley scored seven nominations for that hit and her sophomore album Dandelion. Plus, she's the first country artist since Bobbie Gentry in 1968 to be nominated in each of the big four Grammy awards (album of the year, record of the year, song of the year and best new artist) in a single year, according to Billboard.
The hit you might know: Choosin’ Texas.
Geese

A Brooklyn-based rock quartet fronted by singer/guitarist Cameron Winter, who's also a critically acclaimed solo artist. Geese formed in 2016 and is known for its experimental punk sound, often compared to acts like the Strokes and the Velvet Underground. The group earned a bunch of coverage earlier this year for its marketing team's efforts. Oh, and according to fans, Geese's Saturday Night Live performance of Trinidad is one to watch. The group is up for five trophies, including for the songs Trinidad and Au Pays du Cocaine, as well as their album Getting Killed.
The hit you might know: Au Pays du Cocaine.
Remi Wolf

Remi Wolf isn't your typical pop star — the California artist is known for her high energy and funky basslines, carving out her own lane of soul-infused pop. She actually competed on American Idol in 2014 as a high school senior and broke through with her 2020 EP I'm Allergic to Dogs! Pulling in millions of streams and performing on massive festival and arena stages, she's constantly reinventing herself. And her latest work, Mud, leans a bit more into an indie rock sound.
The hit you might know: Photo ID.
Sienna Spiro

Sienna Spiro has that soulful James Bond theme song sound. She leans into a soulful, jazzy vintage sound in the vein of Adele and Amy Winehouse. The London-based singer-songwriter started posting videos of covers on TikTok in 2021, catching the eyes of major labels before releasing her debut single Need Me in 2024. It was her hit single Die on This Hill that really put her on the map.
The hit you might know: Die on This Hill.
Slayyyter

Take electric dance pop music, cover it in sequins, glitter and a whole lot of gloss, and then throw in a heavy rock edge — that’s what Slayyyter is all about. Her most recent album leans into the early-2000s indie sleaze sound — though she nearly walked away from the industry entirely before making it. Instead of quitting, she put those frustrations into this new record, earning her four Grammy nominations, including best dance/electronic album and recording, as well as best dance pop recording.
The hit you might know: DANCE...
The Womack Sisters

Big stages run in the family for Zeimani, Zekkujcha (Kucha) and Zekuumba (BG) Womack. Their family tree says it all: daughters of Linda and Cecil Womack (of Womack & Womack), nieces of R&B icon Bobby Womack and grandchildren of the legendary Sam Cooke. After spending over a decade performing as backing vocalists for artists like Solange Knowles and releasing music independently, the trio signed to a label in 2025. They followed it with their breakthrough, self-titled debut album, rooted in classic soul and R&B.
The hit you might know: If I Let You.
